newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kazakhstan may pay Russia debts with shares.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan may pay Russia debts with shares.

text.p: Kazakhstan does not rule out paying off some of its growing debts to Russia with shares of some of its large firms, a Kazakh government official said on Tuesday.

"Kazakhstan will have to pay its huge debts to Russia in any case. It would be good to clear some part of these debts by selling shares in some of our companies to Russia," Yuzef Duberman, Deputy Chairman of Kazakhstan's State Privatisation Committee, told a news conference.

Last week Anatoly Dyakov, President of Unified Energy System (UES) EESR.RTS, Russia's national electricity generator, told Reuters that Russia had cut electricity deliveries to most of Kazakhstan because of debts approaching $500 million.

Dyakov said RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) had offered to take Kazakh assets, such as power stations, or part of the coal basin near the town of Ekibastuz in payment of some of Kazakhstan's electricity debts.

"I think the position of UES is reasonable...It is not justified technologically to sell UES just one part of the whole basin," Duberman said. "But UES, alongside other foreign investors, could set up a consortium to exploit its part of the basin. In general, it would be good to clear other debts of Kazakhstan to Russia in a similar way."
